desc:
In one operation you pick two different elements of nums whose values add up to exactly k and remove both from the array.

Return the maximum number of operations you can perform.

nums = [1, 2, 3, 4], k = 5
(1,4) then (2,3)  ->  result = 2

nums = [3, 1, 3, 4, 3], k = 6
only one pair of 3s can be used  ->  result = 1
hints: Each element can be used at most once, so this is about matching elements with their complements k - x.
Sort the array. The smallest value can only be matched with exactly one value, k - smallest, and that value is the same whichever copy you take.
Use lo and hi on the sorted array: sum equal to k means one operation, move both; sum too small means a[lo] has no partner left, move lo; sum too large means a[hi] has none, move hi.
editorial: Sort the array and place two pointers at the ends. If a[lo] + a[hi] == k we perform an operation and discard both. If the sum is smaller than k, even the largest remaining value is not enough for a[lo], so a[lo] can never be matched; if it is larger, a[hi] cannot be matched even with the smallest remaining value.

Matching equal pairs greedily is safe because all candidates for a value are interchangeable copies. A hash map of counts gives the same answer in O(n) time but needs O(n) extra space; the sorted two-pointer version needs only the sort.
